criterion_scores.reasoning: The script is largely sound: it parses input safely, builds valid JSON, and keeps the optional adapter separate. I checked the session gating, transcript metrics, record construction, and write paths. The main correctness issue is line 44: the build-touch signal is underinclusive because it only recognizes Edit/Write tool calls, so some legitimate build edits are misreported.

All major sections are present: input gating, disable override, transcript metrics, optional meta enrichment, record emission, append, and optional projection. I did not find a missing required section, TODO stub, or absent referenced file. The only gaps are secondary edge coverage, not a missing core behavior.

Placement and shape match a .claude hook script, and I did not see any house-convention violations such as forbidden prefixes or non-parent-thread write patterns. The script keeps the authoritative local file as the source of truth and only projects derived data outward.

The implementation is lean and avoids obvious duplicate state or ceremony. I checked for tombstoned patterns, hardcoded secrets, and excessive platforming; none are present. The only mild concern is the permissive silent-failure posture in the optional adapter path.

The script has some explanatory comments, but failure visibility is weak in the load-bearing write/projection section. I checked the append and curl paths: both can fail silently, which makes operational problems hard to explain after the fact. That is a real diagnostics shortfall even though the hook is intentionally non-blocking.

defects.description: This only treats Edit/Write tool calls as evidence that build files were touched. Sessions that modify build artifacts through other write-capable tools (for example MultiEdit) will be recorded as untouched, so the telemetry field is incomplete/wrong for a real subset of sessions.

defects.location: lines 80-90, authoritative append and PostHog projection section
defects.description: The authoritative append has no status check, and the projection path below is also swallowed with `|| true`. If the JSONL write fails (permissions, disk full, etc.) or the PostHog capture fails, the hook still exits 0 with no diagnostic trail, so a load-bearing telemetry failure becomes silent.

checks_performed: Checked stdin/session_id gating and the early-exit paths for missing session IDs and disabled hooks.
Reviewed the transcript parsing jq pipelines for tool-use counts, assistant turns, token counts, start time, and build-touch detection.
Checked record assembly for JSON validity, nullable meta fields, and whether the authoritative JSONL append is actually enforced.
Checked the optional PostHog projection path and its error handling / failure visibility.
Checked house-context conventions at the hook path and for any obvious tombstoned patterns or forbidden write paths.
